messages.content:
I implemented the in-memory, event-driven Task Management API in TypeScript using only Node.js built-in modules. The system includes separate services, an event bus, an API router, a main entry point, and a demo script.

What’s included:
- src/event-bus.ts: Simple publish/subscribe EventBus
- src/services/user-service.ts: UserService with in-memory CRUD
- src/services/project-service.ts: ProjectService with CRUD and member management
- src/services/task-service.ts: TaskService with CRUD, assignee handling, and validated status transitions (todo -> in-progress -> done). Publishes events on create/assign/status change/delete.
- src/services/comment-service.ts: CommentService with in-memory storage and event publication on creation
- src/services/notification-service.ts: NotificationService that subscribes to events (task.assigned, task.statusChanged, comment.added.enriched) and creates notifications. It also transforms comment.added into comment.added.needsAssignee for enrichment.
- src/api-router.ts: HTTP API router using Node’s http and url modules. Routes:
  - Users: GET/POST /users, GET/PUT/DELETE /users/:id
  - Projects: GET/POST /projects, GET/PUT/DELETE /projects/:id, POST/DELETE /projects/:id/members
  - Tasks: GET/POST /tasks?projectId=, GET/PUT/DELETE /tasks/:id, PUT /tasks/:id/status, PUT /tasks/:id/assign
  - Comments: GET/POST /comments?taskId=, GET/DELETE /comments/:id
  - Notifications: GET /notifications?userId=, PUT /notifications/:id/read
- src/main.ts: Wires services and event bus, enriches comment.added.needsAssignee with task assignee, starts HTTP server
- src/demo.ts: Demo script that starts the server (on an ephemeral port), creates users, a project, adds members, creates tasks, assigns and transitions tasks, adds a comment, and shows notifications, then marks one as read
- tsconfig.json: TypeScript configuration

Notes:
- Inter-service communication uses the EventBus. No direct cross-service calls occur inside services. For comment -> notification behavior, the main wiring listens to comment.added.needsAssignee and publishes an enriched event comment.added.enriched that the NotificationService uses to notify the assignee.
- All data is stored in-memory (Maps/arrays). No external dependencies.

How to run:
- Start the API server: npx tsx src/main.ts
- Run the demo (starts server on a random port and exercises all features): npx tsx src/demo.ts

Type-checking:
- A tsconfig.json is included. The environment does not have typescript installed, so npx tsc --noEmit cannot run here. The code runs cleanly with tsx, demonstrating functionality end-to-end.
